verdicts.claim: RoomCaptureView is a UIKit UIView (not SwiftUI) that runs the whole room scan UX for you: camera feed, animated real-time outlines of walls/doors/windows/openings/objects, framework coaching text, and a miniature 3D model of the room at the bottom (toggle with isModelEnabled). After you call captureSession.stop() and your delegate returns true from captureView(shouldPresent:error:), the view itself animates the final post-processed room for the user to review; no built-in Done button exists, the app supplies Done/Cancel/Export chrome.
verdicts.reasoning: Fetched Apple doc JSON. RoomCaptureView: declaration '@MainActor @objc @preconcurrency class RoomCaptureView', Inherits From UIKit/UIView, iOS/iPadOS/Mac Catalyst introducedAt 16.0, not deprecated. Overview: the view 'manages the scan process from start to finish', with 'A camera feed', 'Real-time graphic overlays that display on top of physical structures in the room to convey scanning progress', and 'User instructions that explain how to position the device'. isModelEnabled: '@MainActor @preconcurrency var isModelEnabled: Bool { get set }', iOS 16.0, abstract 'displays a miniature rendering of the scanned room at the bottom of its bounds'. init(frame:arSession:) introducedAt 17.0. captureSession is 'var captureSession: RoomCaptureSession! { get }' (read-only) and delegate is 'weak var delegate: (any RoomCaptureViewDelegate)?'; the claim's api block omits get-only and weak but does not misstate usage. RoomCaptureViewDelegate captureView(shouldPresent:error:) (iOS 16.0) returns Bool; docs: if true, the framework processes results, calls captureView(didPresent:error:), and 'The view (RoomCaptureView) displays the scanned room in a 3D rendition that the user can inspect using touch gestures'; default implementation returns true. Minor caveats not amounting to refutation: docs say 'graphic overlays' rather than enumerating walls/doors/windows/openings/objects, and the docs do not explicitly state the absence of a built-in Done button (the member list has no such control; Apple's sample supplies Done/Cancel/Export buttons itself). Note captureSession is get-only, so code must not assign it.

verdicts.claim: House mode: keep one ARSession alive across rooms by calling stop(pauseARSession: false) after each room and run(configuration:) again for the next; then StructureBuilder merges the CapturedRoom array into a CapturedStructure in one coordinate system with duplicate walls removed. Apple recommends a single floor, 1 to 4 bedrooms plus living/kitchen/dining, max ~2,000 sq ft (186 m2), lighting 50 lux or more.
verdicts.reasoning: Fetched Apple doc JSON. RoomCaptureSession.stop(pauseARSession:) is declared 'func stop(pauseARSession: Bool = true)', iOS/iPadOS/Mac Catalyst 17.0, not deprecated. run(configuration:) is iOS 16.0. StructureBuilder is 'class StructureBuilder', iOS 17.0, with init(options:). capturedStructure(from:) is declared 'func capturedStructure(from rooms: [CapturedRoom]) async throws -> CapturedStructure', iOS 17.0; its discussion says it succeeds only when rooms share compatible world space, achieved by passing the same ARSession and calling stop(pauseARSession:) with false, or by relocalizing with a saved ARWorldMap. CapturedStructure is iOS 17.0. The article 'Scanning the rooms of a single structure' says: call stop(pauseARSession:false) after each room, then 'To start the next scan, call run(configuration:) again on the same room-capture session object', then pass the array to StructureBuilder.capturedStructure(from:). The docs do not literally say 'duplicate walls removed'; that comes from WWDC23 session 10192, which presents manual stitching as leaving duplicate walls/objects and StructureBuilder as producing merged walls, doors, windows, openings and objects. The size/lighting guidance is not in the reference docs but is in the WWDC23 10192 transcript verbatim: 'MultiRoom works best for single-floor residential houses, with a typical setup of one to four bedrooms, living room, kitchen, and dining room... maximal total area of 2,000 square feet or around 186 square meters... good lighting of 50 lux or higher'. Caveats, not refutations: (1) the current structure-scanning article states 'Scanned structures support rooms with varying floor heights and rooms that reside on different floors in the building', so single floor is a best-results recommendation from 2023, not a hard limit; (2) WWDC23 code writes StructureBuilder(option: [.beautifyObjects]) but the documented initializer is init(options:), so use the docs spelling; (3) the article's own snippet omits try await, but the declaration is async throws.

verdicts.claim: House mode: keep one ARSession alive across rooms by calling stop(pauseARSession: false) after each room and run(configuration:) again for the next; then StructureBuilder merges the CapturedRoom array into a CapturedStructure in one coordinate system with duplicate walls removed. verdicts.reasoning: Fetched the WWDC23 session 10192 transcript and code. verdicts.claim: Raw LiDAR mesh visualization in RealityKit is one line (depth-colored wireframe), and per-face coverage coloring needs ARMeshAnchor geometry which is fully readable on iOS.
verdicts.reasoning: Apple doc JSON for ARView.DebugOptions.showSceneUnderstanding: abstract 'Display the depth-colored wireframe for scene-understanding meshes', iOS introducedAt 13.4, not deprecated. Real-world use (Apple sample 'Visualizing and interacting with a reconstructed scene', forums thread 654431, GitHub TravisHall/RealityKit-Example-ARMeshAnchor-Geometry) confirms arView.debugOptions.insert(.showSceneUnderstanding) is the one-line visualization, provided the session runs ARWorldTrackingConfiguration with sceneReconstruction set (not automatic by itself). Forum answer confirms the debug colors are a debug-only scheme that is not accessible or customizable, so custom coverage coloring must be built from ARMeshAnchor.geometry (vertices, normals, faces, classification are MTLBuffer-backed and readable on device), e.g. into a MeshResource via MeshDescriptor/LowLevelMesh; the GitHub example does exactly this. No reports of it being macOS-only or broken on iOS 17/18. Practical caveats, not refutations: ARMeshAnchors are re-meshed and faces have no stable IDs across updates, so per-face coverage state must be keyed spatially (e.g. voxel grid) rather than by face index; debug wireframe is for development and not styleable.

open_question_answers.question: Does the iOS 26 SDK (Xcode 26.6) still restrict PhotogrammetrySession to .reduced on iOS 18 devices, or has a newer OS unlocked .medium? Doc JSON today says reduced only; verify in the first CI build with `#if os(iOS)` and a compile check of `.medium` availability.
open_question_answers.answer: Restricted, and settled by docs without a CI build. In the current doc JSON, PhotogrammetrySession.Request.Detail is iOS 17.0+, but the case .medium lists platforms macOS 12.0 and Mac Catalyst 15.0 only, with no iOS entry (same pattern for .full and .raw). .reduced lists iOS 17.0. The enum overview says: 'On iOS, only one detail level, .reduced, is currently supported.' So on iOS, .medium is marked unavailable at compile time in the iOS 26 SDK; no newer OS unlocks it, and nothing changes this for an iOS 18 device. Architecture: hardcode .reduced on device. Offer higher detail only by exporting the image folder to a Mac. Do not spend a CI round trip on it. If the team wants to double-check, compile `_ = PhotogrammetrySession.Request.Detail.medium` inside `#if os(iOS)` and expect an 'unavailable in iOS' error. The .custom case exists in the listing but was not verified for iOS availability here, so do not rely on it without checking its doc JSON.

open_question_answers.question: RoomCaptureView behavior in landscape is undocumented; if landscape is wanted for the viewer only, confirm the scan screen can stay portrait via per-view orientation lock in a SwiftUI app (UIHostingController subclass or AppDelegate supportedInterfaceOrientationsFor).
open_question_answers.answer: Yes, feasible, but it takes UIKit bridging. SwiftUI has no per-view orientation API. Pattern: set Info.plist to portrait plus landscape. Add an AppDelegate via @UIApplicationDelegateAdaptor with a static orientation mask returned from application(_:supportedInterfaceOrientationsFor:) (iOS 6+; the docs say this is intersected with the root or topmost full-screen view controller's supportedInterfaceOrientations). Set the mask to .portrait when the scan screen appears and to .allButUpsideDown for the viewer. Then call UIViewController.setNeedsUpdateOfSupportedInterfaceOrientations() (iOS 16+) on the root view controller, and UIWindowScene.requestGeometryUpdate(.iOS(interfaceOrientations:)) (iOS 16+) to force the rotation back to portrait. Known risk on iOS 18: a forums report says forcing rotation this way re-renders the whole SwiftUI view and resets @State set before the rotation. So keep scan and viewer state in an observable model owned above the view, not in view @State. Simplest robust option: present the scan screen as a fullScreenCover or a UIViewControllerRepresentable-hosted RoomCaptureViewController whose supportedInterfaceOrientations is .portrait, and never force-rotate while a RoomCaptureSession is running. Device test on the iOS 18.3.2 phone: open the viewer in landscape, then open the scan screen. Expect it to come up portrait and stay portrait while you rotate the phone during a scan. Check that the viewer's selection state survives going back.

open_question_answers.question: Whether sharing a whole export folder via ShareLink works as well as UIActivityViewController with a folder URL (Apple's sample shares the folder). Fallback is zipping or sharing the USDZ file alone.
open_question_answers.answer: Unsure, so only an on-device test can settle it. ShareLink (iOS 16+) takes any Transferable, and URL conforms. But developer forum threads report cases where the same file URL fails or gets renamed (for example to .txt over AirDrop) through ShareLink while it works with UIActivityViewController. No Apple documentation or sample shows ShareLink with a directory URL. Expectation: UIActivityViewController with a folder file URL offers AirDrop and Save to Files and sends the folder. ShareLink with a folder URL may show a reduced activity list. Architecture: put a small UIViewControllerRepresentable wrapper around UIActivityViewController behind a single ShareService, so either path can be swapped in. Zip on device as the universal fallback: NSFileCoordinator with the .forUploading reading option produces a zip of a directory with no third-party code. Test: export a folder (USDZ + OBJ + PDF plan). Share it once via ShareLink(item: folderURL) and once via UIActivityViewController([folderURL]), each to AirDrop-to-Mac, Save to Files, and Mail. Record which targets appear and what arrives.

open_question_answers.question: Exact RoomPlan section labels available on iOS 18 (doc JSON lists livingRoom/kitchen/diningRoom; WWDC23 also mentions bedroom and bathroom).
open_question_answers.answer: The doc JSON for CapturedRoom.Section.Label lists six cases: livingRoom, kitchen, diningRoom, bedroom, bathroom, unidentified. Each case, and CapturedRoom.Section itself, is available on iOS 17.0, iPadOS 17.0 and Mac Catalyst 17.0, so all six exist on iOS 18. The earlier 'three labels only' reading was incomplete. Architecture: map these six to Copy.swift strings. Use a default case in the switch, because the enum may gain cases in later SDKs (Swift 5.9 mode warns for non-frozen Apple enums). Let the user rename rooms freely, with the RoomPlan label only as a suggestion.
